tasks.title: Provide validated subscription settings, durable storage and stopped-service deletion
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, settings/store/deletion layer and its tests; R3, R5 subscribers delete (command implementation, entry-point routing in T4), D18, D21 store primitives, R9 notify, R10 data inventory/retention; Counterexamples: subscribers delete, Cleanup boundaries, Root hosting. Pin the merged contract full SHA. Build the complete store schema and synchronous transactional operations, including guarded completion/finalize primitives and durable pass fields; T3 implements the entire fan-out algorithm over them. Expose cleanup cancellation to the lifecycle consumer added in T2. Production service remains off until T4; update the corresponding docs as capabilities land.

acceptance.expected: 0 failing tests; focused coverage is not the gate. Every R3 default/range, missing required setting, off path, key/token and SMTP counterexample has literal expectations. MAX=5 with pending cap unset (1000) or 6 fails exit 2 naming MAX_PENDING; MAX=5/PENDING=5 accepts. Username and password file must be paired; remote TLS none login fails, loopback accepts; s3cret-pw newline trims to s3cret-pw, empty/two-line file fails without content exposure. Timeout values are available for min(configured,60000). Root URL normalizes its trailing slash; /pulse and /pulse/ fail with the literal R9 line before store/lock/listener opens. Off opens no files even in an unwritable state directory.

0 failing tests. A real mkdtemp SQLite store uses mode 0600, WAL, synchronous FULL, secure_delete ON, user_version 1 and all R3 tables/constraints, including persisted passes=0 and next_pass_at=NULL. Other versions are refused. Every mutation is transactional; completion inserts only while the subscription exists, and finalize selects current subscriptions in its event-done transaction. Startup cleanup and the independent 3600000 ms timer run without polling: expiry 86400001 remains at t=86400000, is gone at t=90000000, confirmed rows remain at 10*86400000. Cleanup returns deleted ids for immediate queue cancellation; retention never prunes pending or still-listed events and does not prune before a good read. Second-connection queries find 0 deleted subscription/delivery rows, checkpoint leaves WAL size 0, and file bytes contain no deleted address; busy checkpoints warn without data and retry at cleanup/shutdown.

0 failing tests. Exercise the CLI module directly under its store lock: normalized confirmed and pending addresses delete with deleted 1, repeat yields deleted 0 (exit 0); missing store yields deleted 0 without creating it; held lock exits 2 with existing lock message; invalid a@b exits 1 with the literal invalid-address line; missing/extra args exit 1 with usage: pulse-notify subscribers delete <address>. It reads only state-path/lock settings, works with subscriptions off, prints no address, and deletes delivery rows/checkpoints to WAL size 0. T4 supplies the executable entry-point routing.

T3 adds the incident worker, the two-worker sequence tests and held-fan-out timing variants; T4 wires the modules into main. Do not create an incident-worker placeholder or split its algorithm across tasks.

Real listener on 127.0.0.1:0 follows path 404, method 405/Allow POST, bearer 401 before body (also wrong bearer plus 2 MiB), JSON type 415, size 413 at 1025 bytes, parse/strict validation 400, store failure 503. Answers are contract-validated JSON/no-store/x-pulse-contract 1. subscribe() is non-Promise for queued/known/limited and every valid subscribe returns literal 202 accepted immediately. Lifecycle literals: at 0/600000/1200000 three mails, none at 599999/1800000; tokens rotate, TTL exclusive at last_sent_at+86400000; repeated confirm preserves first confirmed_at; unsubscribe is idempotent, wrong MAC 404, pending cancellation works, fresh generation has a different id and old token cannot affect it. Every notify No enumeration fixture (below limits, L1 with MAX=2/PENDING=2, L2, L3/L4, L5, L6, store error) uses fresh stores and both orders, compares status/all headers except date/body byte-for-byte and checks literal row/mail effects. Valid replies always 202 {"status":"accepted"}; global store error always 503 unavailable. Capacity counter grows by 1 per unknown request and known confirmed id/state remain. Window at 3599999 refuses silently and at 3600000 admits. Immediate-class checks use frozen clock/recording scheduler and held SMTP: 0 response-path timers and no awaited mail. Entire D19 Confirmation queue block runs behind held A attempt (exactly 1 call while blocked): unsubscribe B changes gauge 3 to 2 immediately and only C sends next; cleanup at 90000000 changes gauge to 1 before A resolves; rotating B keeps gauge 3 and sends only the current digest; at exact expiry 86400001 B is dropped while C sends; retry notBefore=1003 does not block B at t=3, and cancelling A gives 0 second attempts. Confirm cancels queued/retry jobs; worker drops confirmed/gone/rotated/expired rows. In-flight unsubscribe does not abort that attempt; timeouts passed to mailer are literal 60000 and 5000. Worker 1 writes nothing on completion and all guard entries are released. Guard unit cases use keyed normalized addresses, fresh per-process salt, owner 1 then 2, late release(1) cannot free owner 2, stop forbids acquire, and no key contains address/local part. Deferred retry/busy jobs preserve order while other ready mailboxes progress.

0 failing tests. Confirmation messages have exactly one To/envelope address, configured-origin confirmation/unsubscribe/notice links (one slash), literal 24/25 hours, specified subject and independently computed stable Message-ID. Token digest only is persisted; unsubscribe HMAC comparison is timing-safe. R7 metrics register only on opt-in; all literal names/help/labels render, including capacity 2, and the existing off exact-text test stays unchanged. A held confirmation gives gauge 1, then success grows exactly 1 before gauge 0; cancelled jobs increment neither mail counter. Queue holds at most 100 jobs, worker makes at most 3 attempts per job, and stop drops waiting jobs and aborts its send without retaining addresses.

All Counterexamples: One send per mailbox, Late completion after delete, Eligibility and privacy, Fan-out failures. Add an optional notifier hook for each successful non-404 manual projection and listedIds, after channel work; production main opts in only in T4. Retain unchanged operator-channel and ledger behavior. This task implements every stage of the incident algorithm together.

Equality confirmed_at=detected_at is eligible, 999 before confirmation at 1000 is not; first enablement seeds 3 visible incidents with 0 sends, later update sends once. Use only public projections, never /admin; no automatic/reminder/warning mail or private fields; two recipients never see each other's address.
